title: physical filling to contextual capacity
parts: caused displacement in a physical frame
definition: An actor physically adds relevant material contents to a distinct container, changing it from below its fixed contextual usable-capacity threshold to meeting or exceeding that same threshold. The caused-displacement dependency describes the actor's movement of added contents into the container, not movement of the container itself. The full-state dependency describes the same container and content criterion at the result phase; ORI:110 is the completed actualization of that result. These are causally linked phases of one filling episode. The container's identity, positive capacity criterion and relevant content kind remain fixed across the transition. The actor need not move the container. No named substance, numerical amount, source, exact route, seal, overflow, intention, ownership or continued fullness is asserted. Adding some contents without reaching capacity does not complete this meaning. Ongoing aspect views filling internally without asserting a completed full result.
constraints: The outer actor is the cause in the exact caused-displacement dependency; its displaced bearer is added material content, distinct from the outer target container.
The outer target is the container of the exact full-state dependency. Its capacity and relevant content criterion apply unchanged before and after filling.

The container is below that threshold before this transition and full at its culmination because of the addition. Shrinking capacity, relabeling existing contents or merely maintaining an already full state is not this transition.
ORI:110 actualizes fullness, not the container, actor or content kind. Time, negation, modality, aspect and runtime scope the entire linked episode.
excludes: Partial addition presented as a completed filling
An already full state without the required transition
Changing the capacity or relevant kind to declare the container full
Digital storage, completing a form, satisfying a role or emotional fulfillment
A specific substance, quantity, overflow or continued result inferred without being supplied
near: Nora added a little water, leaving the bottle below capacity.
reuse: Reuse this filling event before specifying its material content, source, amount, route or maintained result.
everyday: Adds physical contents until the container reaches its contextual capacity

title: physical removal of relevant container contents
parts: caused displacement in a physical frame
definition: An actor physically removes the relevant material contents from a distinct container, changing it from having some such contents to having none under the same fixed contextual content criterion. The caused-displacement dependency describes the actor's movement of those contents out of the container, not destruction or movement of the container's own body. The empty-state dependency describes the same container and content criterion at the result phase; ORI:110 is the completed actualization of that absence. These are causally linked phases of one emptying episode. The container remains the same material object, and its positive capacity and relevant content kind remain fixed. Contents of irrelevant kinds, such as air in a bottle emptied of water, may remain. No destination, disposal, cleaning, vacuum, named substance, intention, ownership change or continued emptiness is asserted. Removing only some relevant contents does not complete this meaning. Ongoing aspect views emptying internally without asserting a completed empty result.
constraints: The outer actor is the cause in the exact caused-displacement dependency; its displaced bearer is removed relevant material content, distinct from the outer target container.
The outer target is the container of the exact empty-state dependency, with the same capacity and relevant content criterion in both phases.

Some relevant contents are present before the transition and none remain at culmination because of their removal. The container's body persists; destroying contents in place or changing what counts is not this removal.
ORI:110 actualizes emptiness, not the actor or container. All nested phases remain inside the event's tense, negation, modality, aspect and runtime interpretation.
excludes: Partial removal presented as a completed emptying
An empty state without prior relevant contents and their removal
Destroying the container or annihilating contents in place
A vacuum, cleaning, disposal destination or continued result inferred from emptiness
Deleting digital items, emotional depletion or emptying an abstraction
near: Mira removed one item but relevant contents remained in the box.
reuse: Reuse this emptying event before adding a removal destination, disposal, a named content kind or a maintained result.
everyday: Physically removes all relevant contents while preserving the container
